notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Chain fallible steps with `with`. It now opens "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and adds "Count the `<-` clauses before writing `with`. With one there is nothing to chain, and a `with` makes the reader look for the other steps, so use `case`, which shows both outcomes in one place. When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, under the rule heading). The rule is newly listed for this case, so every run gets a verdict. Violating runs out of 5: one-step sentence 1 (sonnet-1, line 222: with {:ok, users} <- parse_user_limits(Map.get(decoded, "users", %{})) do); nested-case clause of the same paragraph 0; else sentence (unchanged) 0. In the previous sweep 1 of 5 runs (sonnet-2) had one-step with blocks, then listed under other_violations; in check-2, 0 of 4.

Three calls decided the with counts. Four runs (haiku-1 lines 115-117, haiku-2 lines 162-164, sonnet-1 lines 201-203, sonnet-2 lines 141-143) write a two-step with whose body returns parse_limits/1, a third fallible call; the second-step sentence speaks only of a one-step with, and nothing is nested or put in an else, so none is counted. Sonnet-1's init/1 with ends in else / {:error, reason} -> {:stop, reason} (lines 149-150); it only rewraps the reason in the tuple init/1 must return, as check-2 ruled for the same else, so it is not counted. Haiku-2's moduledoc controller (lines 37-50) has an else with two clauses that turn the rate-limit error and the changeset error into responses; each step's error already has its own shape and nothing is relabelled, so it is not the large else that maps errors back to steps.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming. The fetch bullet now ends "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." and the variable bullet ends "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## Naming). Violating runs out of 5 per sentence: CamelCase and snake_case 0; application namespace 0 (every module is under MyApp or MyAppWeb); boolean functions end in ? and is_ only for guards 0 (opus's defguardp is_limit/1 and sonnet-2's valid_limit?/1 follow it); get/fetch 1 (sonnet-1's fetch_config_path/1 returns {:error, :missing_config_path}; it does not check the value, so the unchanged first half, "`fetch` returns `{:ok, value}` or `:error`", decides, as check-2 ruled for fetch_required/2 in webhook-parser); size/length 0 (not exercised; the counting helpers are named count_*); ignored values 0; domain variable names 0. Not counted, as before: haiku-1's acc (line 131) and key for a request's ETS key (line 52), haiku-2's objects for ETS rows (line 178), and opus's result for a match spec's result term (line 247). The new variable sentence decides nothing here.

All five runs read the limits file inside init/1: opus-1 line 138 (File.read at line 192), haiku-1 line 68 (line 115), haiku-2 line 122 (line 162), sonnet-1 lines 134-135 (line 208), sonnet-2 line 109 (line 148). Opus-1 (lines 135-137) and haiku-2 (lines 120-121) explain in a comment that this is deliberate, so a bad file stops the boot. The responsive rule is unchanged and names only HTTP calls and large queries as slow work, so as in the previous sweep no verdict rests on it, but every run misses the case's init check. All five start_link/1 functions accept :name (opus-1 line 89, haiku-1 line 35, haiku-2 line 90, sonnet-1 line 126, sonnet-2 line 75), and in a scratch run each started a second instance under name: :other that kept its own count.

All five runs keep per-user request rows in an ETS table owned by the GenServer and write it from the caller with insert-then-count, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are clean in all five; in the previous sweep both Haiku runs kept every count in GenServer state behind GenServer.call and violated both. Branching, Comments and the five process rules are unchanged since 93873be and graded to the previous sweep's standard: start_link options documented under ## Options in @moduledoc are listed under Group related parameters, as for the previous sweep's skill-sonnet-2; missing docs on example modules and the caller examples kept in comments (haiku-1) are not counted.

Each file was formatted, compiled and run in a scratch copy. All five pass mix format --check-formatted. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with no warnings. Haiku-1 warns that Jason.decode/1 is undefined because Jason is not installed (tested with a stub over JSON.decode/1). Opus-1's full file fails because its example plug, controller and worker need Plug, Phoenix and Oban; lines 1-277 compile alone with no warnings. In every run a 50-task burst for one user admitted exactly 2 at a limit of 2 and 5 at a limit of 5, and a sweep removed an expired row and kept a fresh one. Two correctness defects outside the graded rules: sonnet-1's retry_after/3 raises Enum.EmptyError when racing rejected checks have deleted every row (3 of 2000 four-way bursts at a limit of 1), and sonnet-2 counts 7 and "7" as different users, so one user can get twice the limit.
